input.title: Hedgerow: meter exposure on the GPU
input.name: hedgerow-gpu-metering
input.prompt:
First step, before reading any code: your worktree is cut from main, but this task builds on the local branch `perf/hedgerow`, so run `git merge perf/hedgerow` in your worktree (it should fast-forward or merge cleanly) and confirm with `git log --oneline -6` that commits `e0ec399d` through `f08e5ac2` are present. Then:

Remove the exposure-metering stall in Hedgerow. Exposure is metered in `fun/hedgerow/js/adapt.js` (called from `fun/hedgerow/js/main.js`) by reading a 32×18 RGBA8 render target back to the CPU through three's `readRenderTargetPixelsAsync`. On Chrome with ANGLE Metal the `getBufferSubData` behind that read blocks the main thread about 13 times per 3 s, median 70–80 ms, which is 28% of main-thread time and the cause of the 75–80 ms frame spikes. A fence-polled readback was tried on 2026-10-23 and still blocked, because Chrome waits for every frame in flight, so the fix is to meter on the GPU: reduce the metering target to the weighted statistic `adapt.js` computes today (read its code for the exact weighting and median) in a shader pass or a small reduction chain, keep the result in a 1×1 texture, and feed the exposure from it, either sampled directly in the tone-mapping pass or read back no more than once a second without blocking the frame.

Done means the adaptation behaves the same: in a headless real-GPU run of `/fun/hedgerow/index.html?debug&go&god` (wait for `[data-loading]` hidden, click `[data-action="start"]`), the exposure trace over the first 30 s, standing at spawn and then after a flare launched with `G.flares.launchNow(G.camera.position)`, matches the current branch within a few percent at every sample; the profile shows no `getBufferSubData` stall over 5 ms; the ten Node checks pass (`node fun/hedgerow/tests/<name>-check.mjs` from the worktree root: world, route, character, ragdoll, distance, lod, ai, fp, clutter, daze); and the look is unchanged. Beware that the terrain material already uses all 16 fragment samplers, so adding a texture to scene materials will not link on 16-unit GPUs: sample the exposure texture in the post pass only. Report frame-time median and p95 and stall counts before and after.

Five agents ran, one per live game on the site, and their work sits on five local branches cut from `origin/main`. I verified every branch myself: only the game's own directory is touched, the worktree was clean, and the game's full Node check suite passes. Nothing is pushed, and your checkout on `transport-playability` is exactly as I found it.

**Scope decisions.** Transport was skipped: main removed it from the site on 2026-10-19. The three games on disk here were not used either, because this checkout's branch is fully merged and hundreds of commits behind main (alpen alone differs by 26k lines), so each agent worked in a sparse worktree of `origin/main`. Opus handled the three three.js games and Sonnet the two 2D games.

**Results per branch**

| Branch | Commits | Fixes | Performance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `perf/hedgerow` | 5 | Empty particle systems re-uploaded their whole buffers every frame (WebGL2 reads a zero-length range as "to the end") | Render CPU 9.6 → 7.4 ms mean; vegetation upload 4.1 MB → 0.27 MB per refill; idle shadow lights skip their cube maps |
| `perf/alpen` | 3 | Fall-scrape powder scaled with refresh rate (2.4× at 144 Hz) | Terrain point queries −27%, mesh build −6%, bit-identical terrain |
| `perf/ashline` | 8 | Camera moved backwards for one frame after launch or resume | Sim tick at 2,000 units: March 73 → 52 ms, Battle 80 → 51 ms, Harvesting 54 → 43 ms; identical digests; deploy 3.5 → 3.0 s |
| `perf/meteora` | 8 | Restart during the Heart of the Mother flares opened them in the new flight; `tools/bench.mjs` crashed | Sim step 80 → 60 µs, garbage 97 → 51 KB per step; explosion GCs 105 → 3 per 30 s; culler −30%; all bit-identical |
| `perf/tyran` | 3 | GPU textures of dropped sprites were never freed: 12 sectors grew the cache to its 246 MB cap and forced 315 batch-flushing evictions; now 64 MB and none | Per-frame cost was already at its floor and is unchanged |

**What was not verified.** No screenshots were inspected by eye on any branch. Hedgerow, alpen and meteora each had one headless real-GPU run with no console errors, and ashline and tyran ran their relevant Playwright checks, but a visual regression would only show up when you play them.

**Investigated and left alone.** Hedgerow's exposure metering stalls the main thread about 75 ms, 13 times per 3 seconds, and a fence-polled readback still blocked on Chrome's Metal backend, so it needs GPU-side metering. A texture-unit warning in hedgerow turned out to be a false alarm, though the terrain shader now sits at the 16-sampler limit. An A* rewrite for ashline reproduced every path over 8,800 queries but gained only 5%, so it stayed out. Those larger items are the three cards above.

**Cost.** Roughly 2.5 million subagent tokens across the five agents and their follow-ups, about 500k per game.

You are a dispatched subagent (ignore any "superpowers" skill preamble in your context). Task: move Alpen's terrain mesh build off the main thread, in the static site repository protocodus.github.io (GitHub Pages; plain ES modules, no build step, no third-party runtime except vendored three.js under `assets/vendor/three/`).

## Where to work (strict)
- Your private git worktree is `WT = REDACTED` on branch `alpen-terrain-worker`, a sparse checkout (only `fun/alpen`, `assets/` and root files) cut from the local branch `perf/alpen`, which already holds a 2026-10-23 perf pass (cheaper terrain row contexts for point queries, V8-exact inlined hypot in the mesh build, a refresh-rate fix for fall-scrape powder). It is clean. Work ONLY there and edit ONLY files under `WT/fun/alpen/`.
- Run every git command as `git -C <WT> …`. Never run git commands in `/Users/vojta/Dev/protocodus.github.io` and never read code from it (stale). Never use `git stash`, `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- .` or `git clean` anywhere.
- Commit on `alpen-terrain-worker` only (one commit per logical step, `perf(alpen): …`, body with measured numbers, ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`). Do not push, do not open PRs.
- The disk is nearly full (about 3 GB free): keep temporary files small, write them under `WT/../alpen-tmp/` (create it), delete CPU profiles and screenshots once read, and never leave anything in the repo outside `fun/alpen/`.

## The task
The terrain mesh build in `fun/alpen/js/terrain.js` (`createTerrain`, with `fillHeightRows` and `fillSurfaceRows` generating chunk rows from the seeded height functions, `rowContext`, `heightIn`, `wallFields`, `hazardFields`) is the dominant main-thread cost: about 0.95 ms per frame on average with 4 ms slices while a chunk builds on an M1 Max, and several times that on phones (Alpen supports touch and mobile rendering). `fun/alpen/js/shadow-worker.js` with `shadow-cache.js` already shows how this game offloads work to a Worker.

Done means: chunk rows are generated in a Worker (or the existing worker pattern) from the same seeded functions, transferred as typed arrays, and applied on the main thread, with bit-identical results. Prove it with a deterministic 60 s streaming ride that gives the same SHA-1 for every mesh buffer as the main-thread build (commit `58bf7804` on this branch describes such a harness; `git -C <WT> show 58bf7804` shows what it measured). All eight checks must pass, run from `WT/fun/alpen`: `node tests/riding-check.mjs`, `touch-input-check`, `flow-check`, `terrain-shadow-check`, `models-check`, `graphics-check`, `mobile-render-check`, `hud-check` (`tests/README.md` says what each pins; `terrain-shadow-check` pins terrain continuity and determinism). A chunk must arrive before the rider reaches it: keep a synchronous fallback when it would not, and keep the first chunks synchronous if that is what makes the start robust. Keep the vendored three.js, plain ES modules and no build step. The worker must import the same `terrain.js`, `noise.js` and `config.js` modules (ES module worker), so factor out any DOM or three.js dependence at their module scope instead of duplicating code; `terrain.js` imports `three` by the bare specifier through the page's import map, which a worker does not have, so handle that (for example a worker-safe module split, or passing a URL) without duplicating the height code. Measure main-thread ms per frame and the worst frame while streaming before and after, headlessly, and report both. Do not change terrain shape, props density or gameplay.

## Method
1. Orient: `git -C <WT> log --oneline -4`, `tests/README.md`, the structure of `createTerrain` (grep for `fillHeightRows`, `fillSurfaceRows`, `rowContext`, `requestChunk`/the streaming scheduler in `terrain.js` and `main.js`), `shadow-worker.js`/`shadow-cache.js` for the worker pattern. Grep first; read targeted line ranges rather than whole 4,000-line files.
2. Baseline: run all eight checks; build the SHA-1 harness (Node, the real modules, a deterministic 60 s ride) and record the main-thread cost per frame and worst frame of the current build.
3. Implement; keep the on-main-thread path available (fallback and the Node checks run without a browser Worker).
4. Verify: checks, SHA-1 equality, before/after numbers; one short real-GPU headless run (below) to confirm the game boots and streams with the worker active and no console errors.
5. Commit; report.

## Environment notes
- Node v26, Python 3.11. Bash runs zsh inside a macOS sandbox: brace variables before a colon (`"${x}:y"`), never name a variable `path`.
- Chromium cannot launch inside the sandbox (Mach port check-in denied): for any Playwright/browser command set `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on that Bash call. `$TMPDIR` differs between sandboxed and unsandboxed calls, so use absolute paths under `WT/..` for anything shared.

Chrome for Testing with a real GPU: executablePath `REDACTED Chrome for Testing.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome for Testing`, args `--use-angle=metal --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist`, `headless: true`. Never run a WebGL game under SwiftShader. Serve `WT` with `python3 -m http.server 8701 --bind 127.0.0.1` in the background; use port 8701 only; module workers need the page served, not file://.
- Headless only; never open a visible browser; never use the user's Chrome profile. Before finishing, stop every server and browser you started and confirm with `lsof -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN -P` (`ps` is blocked in the sandbox).

## Report (final message, ≤ 450 words)
1. Baseline numbers and checks. 2. Design: what runs in the worker, how chunks are scheduled, the fallback. 3. Before→after main-thread ms per frame and worst frame; SHA-1 equality evidence. 4. Verification: checks, GPU run, what was not seen. 5. Commits (hash + subject) on `alpen-terrain-worker`. 6. Not done / risks. 7. Approximate tool-call count.

"""Apply the GPU exposure-metering change to the hedgerow worktree: adapt.js (new file), the grade
in post.js (multiplies the eye's factor in), main.js (attaches the eye to the grade) and the README."""
import os, shutil, sys
WT = 'REDACTED'
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
os.chdir(WT)
shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(HERE, 'adapt.gpu.js'), 'js/adapt.js')
print('copied js/adapt.js')

def patch(path, edits):
    s = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    for old, new in edits:
        n = s.count(old)
        assert n == 1, f"{path}: anchor found {n} times: {old[:70]!r}"
        s = s.replace(old, new)
    open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
    print('patched', path, len(edits), 'edits')

patch('js/post.js', [
 ("uniform sampler2D tSrc;\nuniform float uTime, uHurt, uFlash, uSat, uGrain, uAspect, uSharp, uContrast;",
  "uniform sampler2D tSrc;\nuniform sampler2D tAdapt;      // the eye (adapt.js): its exposure factor, one pixel\nuniform float uTime, uHurt, uFlash, uSat, uGrain, uAspect, uSharp, uContrast;"),
 ("  col += col * g * gk + g * 0.005;\n  gl_FragColor = vec4(max(col, 0.0), 1.0);",
  "  col += col * g * gk + g * 0.005;\n  // the eye's exposure (adapt.js), here where the tone mapping that follows would have scaled by it\n  col *= texture2D(tAdapt, vec2(0.5)).r;\n  gl_FragColor = vec4(max(col, 0.0), 1.0);"),
 ("  geometry.setAttribute('uv', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute([0, 2, 0, 0, 2, 0], 2));\n  const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({\n    vertexShader: VERT, fragmentShader: FRAG,\n    uniforms: {\n      tSrc: { value: null }, uTime: { value: 0 }, uHurt: { value: 0 }, uFlash: { value: 0 },",
  "  geometry.setAttribute('uv', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute([0, 2, 0, 0, 2, 0], 2));\n  // the eye wide open, until an adaptation is attached (`adaptation`, set by main.js)\n  const open = new THREE.DataTexture(new Float32Array([1, 1, 1, 1]), 1, 1, THREE.RGBAFormat, THREE.FloatType);\n  open.minFilter = open.magFilter = THREE.NearestFilter;\n  open.needsUpdate = true;\n  const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({\n    vertexShader: VERT, fragmentShader: FRAG,\n    uniforms: {\n      tSrc: { value: null }, tAdapt: { value: open }, uTime: { value: 0 }, uHurt: { value: 0 }, uFlash: { value: 0 },"),
 ("    enabled: true, needsSwap: true, uniforms: material.uniforms,",
  "    enabled: true, needsSwap: true, uniforms: material.uniforms,\n    adaptation: null,               // adapt.js: the eye whose exposure factor the grade applies"),
 ("      material.uniforms.tSrc.value = readBuffer.texture;",
  "      if (this.adaptation) material.uniforms.tAdapt.value = this.adaptation.texture;\n      material.uniforms.tSrc.value = readBuffer.texture;"),
])
patch('js/main.js', [
 ("    // the eye adapting to a flare (adapt.js): the exposure closes down when the view brightens\n    adapt = createAdaptation({ base: renderer.toneMappingExposure });",
  "    // the eye adapting to a flare (adapt.js): the exposure closes down when the view brightens; the\n    // grade applies its factor, found and kept on the GPU (nothing is read back)\n    adapt = createAdaptation({ base: renderer.toneMappingExposure });\n    grade.adaptation = adapt;"),
])
patch('README.md', [
 ("""    `adapt.js` the eye adapting (the frame metered just ahead of the grade:
    the median of its log luminance over 32 x 18 patches, read back a few
    frames later without stalling, and only once the mission is under way; the exposure closes down within half
    a second when a flare bursts and the whole view brightens, opens up
    again over a few seconds, never past the night's own, and holds still
    through a lightning stroke) ·""",
  """    `adapt.js` the eye adapting (the frame metered just ahead of the grade:
    the median of its log luminance over 32 x 18 patches, found on the GPU
    and kept there in a one-pixel texture the grade multiplies in, so nothing
    is ever read back to stall the frame, and only once the mission is under way; the exposure closes down within half
    a second when a flare bursts and the whole view brightens, opens up
    again over a few seconds, never past the night's own, and holds still
    through a lightning stroke) ·"""),
])
print('done')

---
name: hedgerow-gpu-findings
description: "Hedgerow GPU facts from the 2026-10-23 perf pass: exposure metering now GPU-side on branch hedgerow-gpu-metering, the shader warm-up stubs renderer.render, the terrain shader sits at the 16-sampler limit"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Found on 2026-10-23 while optimizing Hedgerow (fun/hedgerow) headlessly on the M1 Max under Chrome for Testing with ANGLE Metal:

- **Exposure metering readback stalled the main thread.** `adapt.js` metered exposure through three's `readRenderTargetPixelsAsync` on a 32×18 target; the `getBufferSubData` behind it blocks even after its fence signals (Chrome on ANGLE Metal waits for every frame in flight): at 120 fps, 422 reads in 30 s, 398 over 5 ms, 3.65 s blocked. Fixed on local branch `hedgerow-gpu-metering` (commit f2813bc7, based on `perf/hedgerow`): the weighted median is found by a rank pass on the GPU, the eye's state (factor, target, metered) lives in a 1×1 float texture eased in a shader, and the grade in `post.js` multiplies the factor in just ahead of three's tone mapping (same product as `toneMappingExposure`). Zero readbacks after; exposure within 0.5% of the old code.
- **The shader warm-up in `main.js` (`warmShaders`) runs the effects chain once with `renderer.render` replaced by a stub** that only records and compiles, with 4×4 buffers. A pass that keeps state on the GPU must not treat that call as a real draw: the adaptation writes its wide-open initial state every frame until it has metered once (`primed`). The warm-up's tail compiles every ShaderMaterial created so far (`madeShaders`), so new pass materials need no special registration.
- **The terrain fragment shader uses all 16 samplers** (9 splat maps, tSward, tRut, envMap, dfgLUT, one flare shadow map, two lamp cube shadow maps; tCanopy is a 17th in the vertex shader). three warns "Trying to use 16 texture units while this GPU supports only 16" because it compares against the fragment limit; the combined limit is 32 and everything is sampled. One more fragment texture or shadow light on that material will stop it linking on 16-unit GPUs; packing the four splat normal maps into a texture array would free three slots.
- **Draw-call counts hide empty-mesh gains**: three's `renderer.info` does not count zero-instance draws; compare `renderer.render` CPU time instead.
- **Headless measurement recipe that worked**: Playwright + Chrome for Testing (`--use-angle=metal --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist`, headless), files served through `page.route` from the worktree (no server process), `?debug&go&god`, wait for `[data-loading]` hidden, click `[data-action="start"]`, then `hedgerow.G` (renderer, camera, flares.launchNow) and `hedgerow.fx.adapt`; wrap `WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype.getBufferSubData` and `requestAnimationFrame` in an init script to time stalls and frames. `hedgerow.G` and `fx.adapt` are null for a moment after the loading screen hides.

**How to apply:** when a Hedgerow frame-time question comes up, these are the known ceilings and traps; see [[verify-headlessly]] for the general headless recipe and [[stale-checkout-base-on-origin-main]] for the worktree setup.

All three follow-up tasks are finished and verified. Nothing is pushed, and the checkout, which is now on `main` and clean, was not touched.

**Hedgerow: exposure metered on the GPU** (commit f2813bc7 on `hedgerow-gpu-metering`, on top of `perf/hedgerow`). The weighted median is found by a rank pass, the eye's state lives in a one-pixel texture eased in a shader, and the grade multiplies the factor in where tone mapping would have applied it. Same headless conditions, before → after:

| | Old readback | GPU metering |
|---|---|---|
| Blocking reads per 30 s | 422 (3.65 s blocked) | 0 |
| Frame median / p95 / max | 8.3 / 8.9 / 17.3 ms | 8.3 / 9.0 / 9.4 ms |
| Exposure vs old code | | within 0.47%, mean 0.08% |

One trap was found on the way: the game's shader warm-up runs the effects chain with `renderer.render` stubbed, so a pass with GPU state must not treat that call as a real draw. The eye now writes its wide-open state every frame until it has metered once.

**Tyran: sector-entry hitches** (5 commits on `tyran-sector-hitches`, on top of `perf/tyran`). Fleet and effect artwork is built in small steps on the warm queue, the flame sheet is built once, and texture-allocation checks in background jobs wait on a fence instead of stalling. Title-screen sector choice: worst task 128 → 14 ms, worst frame 133 → 17 ms, no frames over 25 ms. Shop: ready after 828 → 245 ms. The first flight frame is pixel-identical in all 31 entries compared. A cold `launch` still takes about 200 ms in one task because the preload and recovery checks require a complete sector at return.

**Alpen: terrain build in a worker** (commit 7647eb2a on `claude/wonderful-albattani-82224d`, which also contains `perf/alpen`). This came from the session you restarted, so I checked it myself: all nine alpen checks pass, including its new worker check, and a headless browser boot shows the terrain worker running with no errors.

**Branches.** Five pull requests would cover everything, since three branches contain their predecessors: `perf/ashline`, `perf/meteora`, `hedgerow-gpu-metering`, `tyran-sector-hitches`, and the alpen session's branch. All merge cleanly onto today's main. Main also gained two new games today, Zipper and Patcher, which no agent has reviewed; that is the card above.

**Not seen by eye.** All verification was headless: Node checks, digests, and traces. Visuals were compared by numbers, not by looking.
